introduction: The guide is a hundred small prayers and promises of prayer, almost all of them for a named person: a child at school, a father who has died, a sister, a prisoner, a city, a woman who set a table. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá rises thinking of people and prays for them at midnight; he also asks them to pray for him. Intercession of this kind fills the letters of Paul, who makes mention of his friends without ceasing, and the Qur’án’s prayers for parents and offspring; Moses prays for his sister, Hector for his son, Monica asks to be remembered at the altar, Lincoln writes to a bereaved mother. Because the practice is so natural, its critics are few and worth hearing: Emerson, who called prayer for particular things vicious, the Articles that feared prayers for the dead, Mark Twain on the unspoken half of a prayer for our side, and Jesus’s question about greeting one’s brethren only.
questions: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays for others what he prays for himself, and asks for their prayers in return. What does it change between two people when each knows the other prays for them?

Many of these prayers ask forgiveness for parents who have died. Set the Qur’án’s prayers and Monica’s request beside the Article that rejects such practices. What do you think these prayers do, for the dead and for the living?
Emerson calls prayer for “a particular commodity” vicious; the readings ask for success at school, safe travel and relief from grief. How would you defend asking for particular things?
Most of the prayers are for members of one community. Where do the readings reach beyond it, and how does Jesus’s “if ye salute your brethren only” bear on your own praying?
Things are done “on your behalf”: a jug of water carried, earth moved, a shrine visited. Can one person’s act stand for another’s, and what makes it more than a kind gesture?
Confucius, offered a prayer in his illness, said “my praying has been for a long time.” In what sense might a life be a prayer for others?

outside.why: Asked to pray for someone’s protection from the insistent self, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says he prays the same for himself. Jesus’s prayer for his friends: I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.

A prayer to be protected from one’s own self. Marcus Aurelius recommends prayers of that kind over the usual ones: another prays, how shall I be released from this? Pray thou, how shall I not desire to be released?
He prays at midnight for three people who worked hard at publishing. Paul: remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love.
“Every morning I rise from my bed thinking of you.” Paul to the Ephesians: I cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers.
A prayer that someone may become as God wishes, “because God always loves those who repent.” Jesus: there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
He asks pardon for a friend and for himself together. James: confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another.
“Do beseech and pray constantly for ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.” Paul asks the same of people he has not yet met: strive together with me in your prayers to God for me.
The Báb, in solitude, hopes that others “may supplicate unto Thee on my behalf.” The writer to the Hebrews: pray for us, that I may be restored to you the sooner.
The one who prays for others hopes they will “share and participate” with him in servitude. Jesus: whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.
A prayer is written out for someone to say. Socrates ends a conversation with one of his own, give me beauty in the inward soul, and his friend answers: ask the same for me.
“This servant is present and attaining in thy stead.” Paul of Onesimus: that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me.
Those “deprived of meeting Thee” are prayed the reward of those who attained. The First Letter of Peter to such people: whom having not seen, ye love.
A believer prepares a room in the prison and invites his Lord. The letter to Laodicea: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him.
At the shrine he “beseeched forgiveness for those who have ascended.” Judas Maccabeus made an offering for his fallen soldiers, in that he was mindful of the resurrection.
A visit made “as a representative of yourself.” Monica’s request to her sons: remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you may be.
“I shall carry some loads of earth on thy behalf.” Paul on what one person’s act can be for another: ye also helping together by prayer for us.
A jug of water carried “on your behalf.” Jesus: whosoever shall give to drink a cup of cold water only shall in no wise lose his reward.
A prayer for one “awakened from the sleep of heedlessness.” The hymn in Ephesians: awake thou that sleepest, and Christ shall give thee light.
“Make this little maidservant of Thine blessed and happy.” Children were brought to Jesus that he should put his hands on them, and pray.
Every honour and prosperity is asked “for this family.” A psalm written to be said for someone else: the Lord hear thee in the day of trouble, grant thee according to thine own heart.
A son “seeks pardon for his father.” Abraham’s prayer in the Qur’án: our Lord! Forgive me and my parents and believers on the day when the account is cast.
“Keep Your handmaiden … protected and preserved.” The oldest blessing in the Bible: the Lord bless thee, and keep thee; the Lord make his face shine upon thee.
A child is a hyacinth and a twig in the garden. The psalm of the household: thy children like olive plants round about thy table.
Kindness sent to two children by name. Jacob, with his hands on his grandsons’ heads: the Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads.
A woman is praised as purified, enkindled, and joyful in serving. Proverbs on such a one: strength and honour are her clothing; she openeth her mouth with wisdom.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes the prayer of Zachariah for an heir. Here is the same prayer as another chapter of the Qur’án gives it: my Lord! Bestow upon me of Thy bounty goodly offspring.
“Make the son the mystery of the father.” Hector, lifting his little son before battle, asks more: may men say of him, he is better than his father.
A prayer that thirsting sons be guided. The elder who wrote the Third Letter of John: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
Three boys are prayed for by name. The prayer the Qur’án gives to parents: vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring, and make us patterns for those who ward off evil.
“I hope that Rahim will be successful in his studies.” Daniel and his companions at school in Babylon: God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning.

Success at school and arrangements for a journey are prayed for. Emerson would have none of it: prayer that craves a particular commodity, anything less than all good, is vicious. Is asking for particular things for others open to his objection?
Two men “did not seek to gather worldly goods … but rather sought to dwell near Thee.” The psalmist: one thing have I desired of the Lord, that I may dwell in the house of the Lord.
He “has spent all that he could in Thy path.” Boaz to Ruth: the Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord, under whose wings thou art come to trust.
A company “has arisen to serve Thee and promote sciences.” Paul’s prayer for Colossae: being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God.

“Day and night do I supplicate God in their behalf” for a city. Isaiah’s watchmen: ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, and give him no rest, till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.
A prayer that a youth may speak and write with wisdom. Paul: we do not cease to pray for you, that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding.
“That you may study and be educated.” Paul’s prayer for Philippi: that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment.
“Accept from her this table which she hath spread for Thy loved ones.” Jesus of a woman’s gift: she hath done what she could; this shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.
A prayer for two servants together. The Preacher: two are better than one; for if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow.
A woman who wrote down the talks is prayed for with her daughters. Paul commends Phebe: she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.
“We beseech God to forgive thy father.” Noah’s prayer in the Qur’án: my Lord! Forgive me and my parents and him who entereth my house believing.
“Overlook her shortcomings; confer upon her Thy Grace!” Paul of a friend who had sought him out in prison: the Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day.
Forgiveness is asked for someone’s parents. The Qur’án’s words for a child to say: my Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little.

The readings pray freely for the forgiveness of the dead. The Church of England’s Articles of 1563 rejected the practices that had grown round such prayers as vainly invented and grounded upon no warranty of Scripture. What is it about praying for the dead that could be feared?
“Cause him to enter the paradise of Thy oneness.” Horatio over Hamlet: good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.
“Night and day, engaged in remembering you, and happy with your thought.” Paul: always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy.

He would give his life for each of the friends, and prays for them as lost in the wilderness. Moses for his people: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book.
“Grant him rest in the shade of the tree of pardon.” The Wisdom of Solomon: the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God; they are in peace.
Pardon is asked for the parents of a believer. Dante meets a crowd of shades who only prayed that someone else may pray, so as to hasten their becoming holy.

“The heart was stirred and the spirit was drawn in supplication” for two friends. Tennyson’s dying Arthur to the last of his knights: pray for my soul; more things are wrought by prayer than this world dreams of.
Mercy for a mother and father who have gone before. The Qur’án: our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith.
A servant “hoping for Thy help and protection.” A psalm’s promise: call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee.
“Free [him] from the bonds of grief.” Lincoln to a mother said to have lost five sons: I pray that our Heavenly Father may assuage the anguish of your bereavement.
A prayer for “descendants of the glorious Abraham.” Paul: my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.
Two “protectors of the poor and helpers of the weak.” A psalm: blessed is he that considereth the poor: the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble.
“Pour forth upon them patience from Thee.” The First Letter of Peter: the God of all grace, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.
A lamp “beset by tempestuous winds.” Jesus to Peter: Satan hath desired to have you; but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
A believer “in the hands of the tyrannical.” When Peter was kept in prison, prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.
Bahá’u’lláh prays for his sister. Moses for his: heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.
One who “hath been tried in Thy path.” Paul: we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling.
“These friends … yearn eagerly for the revelation of Thy splendours.” Jesus on the night of his arrest: I pray for them; keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me.
Two who “have chosen tribulation over a life of ease.” Hebrews of Moses: choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.
“Since the day of my departure … I have been always remembering you.” Paul of a friend far from home: always labouring fervently for you in prayers.
A prayer for the Assembly of a city. Paul’s farewell to the elders of Ephesus: I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace.
A prayer that widens from one community to “all the people of that land.” The psalm: God be merciful unto us, and bless us; that thy way may be known upon earth, thy saving health among all nations.
Joy for Iṣfahán and prosperity for Najafábád. The psalmist to his city: for my brethren and companions’ sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee.
“Encompass all his kindred … in honor of him.” The Qur’án gives the angels such a prayer: make them enter the Gardens, with such of their fathers and their wives and their descendants as do right.
A man is prayed for as the kinsman of one who served. Paul to Timothy: without ceasing I have remembrance of thee in my prayers, calling to remembrance the faith which dwelt first in thy grandmother.
“Aid Thy loved ones and Thy branches.” Paul: I bow my knees unto the Father, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, that ye be strengthened with might.
That censure may not deter him. Paul asks his readers to pray for him, that I may open my mouth boldly.
A servant “hoping for Thy bounty, relying upon Thy kingdom.” Ignatius of Loyola’s offering: take, Lord, and receive all my liberty; give me only your love and your grace.
After deserts and seas, the pilgrim’s prayer is short: “Forgive my sins and awaken my heart.” The publican’s was shorter: God be merciful to me a sinner.
Bahá’u’lláh prays for a man by the Prophet, his family and companions. The Qur’án: Allah and His angels shower blessings on the Prophet; O ye who believe, ask blessings on him.
“Cause all who have believed … to enter the kingdom of Thy grace.” Jesus widens his prayer the same way: neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe.
“Join them with Thy servant in servitude.” Paul: the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all men.
He has hastened “to find shelter in Thy shadow.” The psalm: he shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust.
“Honor this poor servant in the Great Kingdom.” The thief on the cross: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
“These brothers are loving, companions and friends.” The psalm: how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
“Make the end of your life the beginning of favors.” The psalmist: now also when I am old and greyheaded, O God, forsake me not.
A prayer that a man may “bring forth righteous offsprings.” Hannah, praying for a child at Shiloh: I have poured out my soul before the Lord.
“Refuge of the weak ones and Shelter of the poor.” A psalm: this poor man cried, and the Lord heard him.
A servant who travels “speaking Your remembrance.” Isaiah: how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace.
God is addressed as the One “Who quickenest the dry and crumbling bone.” Ezekiel in the valley: son of man, can these bones live? O Lord God, thou knowest.
“Be Thou … a friend, a comforter, and a loving companion.” Jesus’s promise: I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever.
One who “has turned his gaze from every direction.” Paul: forgetting those things which are behind, I press toward the mark.
“Make him speak with proof and evidence.” Moses said he was slow of speech, and was answered: I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.
He “changeth sorrows and anguish into gladness and joy.” Isaiah: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
“My hope is that the prayer will be answered.” Jesus: what things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.
A prayer offered for others in hope of an answer. When a disciple asked leave to pray for the sick Confucius, he answered: my praying has been for a long time. What did he mean had been his prayer?
“Protect him from the arrows” of the envious. The psalm of protection: thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night, nor for the arrow that flieth by day.

The prayer is for the one whom the envious lie in wait for. Jesus asks for a second prayer: pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you. Where in these readings is the enemy prayed for?
“Make him a goodly example to all humanity.” Jesus: let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.

A prayer of five short clauses: illumined, heavenly, spiritual, divine. Tolstoy’s three old hermits know only one, three are ye, three are we, have mercy upon us, and the bishop who came to teach them leaves it alone.
“Truth has come and falsehood has perished.” Milton: let her and Falsehood grapple; who ever knew Truth put to the worse, in a free and open encounter?

A prayer that one’s own speaker may have “overwhelming power.” Mark Twain’s stranger tells a congregation what its prayer for victory also asks: when you have prayed for victory you have prayed for many unmentioned results which follow victory. What is the unspoken half of a prayer for our side?
A woman “mentions thee at all times … and offers prayers for thee in the Holy Shrine.” Paul: I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers.

Nearly every prayer in the guide is for a believer or a believer’s family. Jesus presses on that habit: if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? Which readings here reach past the circle?
He “strives to serve Thy servants throughout the worlds.” Coleridge’s mariner: he prayeth best, who loveth best all things both great and small.
“Both outward and inward bounties” for two friends. The elder to Gaius: I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
Letters that were each “a truthful messenger, a blessed courier.” Proverbs: as cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.

ephesians-making-mention-of-you.text: Wherefore I also, after I heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus, and love unto all the saints, Cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers

ephesians-i-bow-my-knees.text: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man

colossians-do-not-cease-to-pray-for-you.text: For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding

thessalonians-increase-and-abound-in-lov.text: And the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all men, even as we do toward you: To the end he may stablish your hearts unblameable in holiness before God, even our Father

thessalonians-pray-always-for-you.text: Wherefore also we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling, and fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness, and the work of faith with power

philemon-mention-of-thee-always.text: I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers, Hearing of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints; That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus

samuel-ceasing-to-pray-for-you.text: Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way

john-i-pray-for-them.text: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are

john-keep-them-from-the-evil.text: I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil

romans-strive-together-in-your-prayers.text: Now I beseech you, brethren, for the Lord Jesus Christ's sake, and for the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together with me in your prayers to God for me

hebrews-pray-for-us.text: Pray for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly. But I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner

corinthians-helping-together-by-prayer.text: Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf

genesis-bless-the-lads.text: And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day, The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth

psalm-the-lord-hear-thee.text: The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee; Send thee help from the sanctuary, and strengthen thee out of Zion; Remember all thy offerings, and accept thy burnt sacrifice; Selah. Grant thee according to thine own heart, and fulfil all thy counsel

psalm-for-my-brethren-and-companions.text: For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee. Because of the house of the Lord our God I will seek thy good

exodus-blot-me-out-of-thy-book.text: And Moses returned unto the Lord, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold. Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written

numbers-heal-her-now.text: And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee

hebrews-ever-liveth-to-make-intercession.text: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them

job-prayed-for-his-friends.text: And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before

psalm-when-they-were-sick.text: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth: I humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer returned into mine own bosom. I behaved myself as though he had been my friend or brother: I bowed down heavily, as one that mourneth for his mother

psalm-god-be-merciful-unto-us.text: God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us; Selah. That thy way may be known upon earth, thy saving health among all nations

peter-stablish-strengthen-settle.text: But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you

ruth-the-lord-deal-kindly-with-you.text: And Naomi said unto her two daughters in law, Go, return each to her mother's house: the Lord deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead, and with me. The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband. Then she kissed them; and they lifted up their voice, and wept

isaiah-give-him-no-rest.text: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth

romans-my-hearts-desire-and-prayer.text: Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved

colossians-epaphras-labouring-in-prayers.text: Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God

acts-commend-you-to-god.text: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified

acts-kneeled-down-and-prayed-with-them.text: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all. And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him, Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship

matthew-brought-little-children.text: Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them. But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven. And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence

quran-zachariah-goodly-offspring.text: Then Zachariah prayed unto his Lord and said: My Lord! Bestow upon me of Thy bounty goodly offspring. Lo! Thou art the Hearer of Prayer.

quran-make-me-to-give-thanks.text: And We have commended unto man kindness toward parents. His mother beareth him with reluctance, and bringeth him forth with reluctance, and the bearing of him and the weaning of him is thirty months, till, when he attaineth full strength and reacheth forty years, he saith: My Lord! Arouse me that I may give thanks for the favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and that I may do right acceptable unto Thee. And be gracious unto me in the matter of my seed. Lo! I have turned unto Thee repentant, and lo! I am of those who surrender (unto Thee).
